strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses generalizable 3D style transfer without per-scene optimization
Thoughtful architecture with clear motivation: separation of geometry (self-attention) and style (cross-attention) pathways is well-justified and shown to be superior
Novel 3D voxel-based style loss: principled extension of 2D statistics matching to 3D space that explicitly incorporates geometric structure
Comprehensive experimental validation: strong results across multiple datasets (CO3D, DL3DV-10K, Tanks & Temples) with multiple metrics; thorough ablations on design choices
Impressive zero-shot generalization: demonstrates transfer to unseen categories, scenes, and styles with single trained model
Strong reproducibility: detailed pseudo-code, public datasets, promised code release, clear methodology
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components are largely existing techniques (VGGT backbone used unchanged, cross-attention follows AdaIN, voxelization from AnySplat); main contribution (3D style loss) is straightforward extension of 2D statistics to 3D

Significant scalability limitations: acknowledged quality degradation beyond 32 views per batch; edge artifacts at 64 views; training-test mismatch (trained with ≤24 views); high memory (10.42 GB at 64 views) and runtime (4.8s per batch) limit practical applicability despite claims of scaling to hundreds of views

Incomplete baseline comparisons: concurrent work (Styl3R) unavailable at submission; unfair comparison setup (per-scene specialized models vs. single generalist model); missing per-scene fine-tuning comparison

Insufficient depth/pose sensitivity analysis: 3D style loss critically depends on accurate depth/camera estimates, but no sensitivity analysis provided; voxelization parameters (resolution, spatial extent) not specified; confidence weighting scheme unclear
Weak ablation on two-stage training: complex training procedure not validated; no single-stage training comparison; color-jittering pseudo-style seems ad-hoc

Limited geometry preservation analysis: claims 'geometry-aware' but mostly keeps geometry frozen from VGGT; reconstruction metrics only in style-free setting; no quantitative analysis of geometric detail preservation during stylization
Missing experimental details: hyperparameter values, voxel resolution selection, spatial extent, convergence criteria, training duration not fully specified
No failure case analysis or discussion of limitations: no analysis of challenging scenarios or when method struggles; limited discussion of method limitations and edge cases

strengths: Well-motivated problem: 3D style transfer without per-scene optimization is practically valuable and clearly articulated
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple datasets (CO3D, DL3DV-10K, Tanks and Temples), diverse metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, consistency measures, ArtScore), and reasonable ablations

Intuitive dual-pathway architecture: Separate handling of geometry (self-attention) and style (cross-attention) is sensible, supported by Table 1 ablation showing global-only outperforms frame-only and hybrid variants
Novel 3D style loss: Extending voxel-space statistics matching to enforce view-consistent stylization is a meaningful contribution with clear spatial reasoning
Strong visual results: Figure 5 demonstrates competitive stylization quality with better geometry preservation than StyleGS and StyleRF
Reproducibility efforts: Includes detailed pseudo-code for loss functions and commits to releasing code upon acceptance
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: Backbone directly uses VGGT unchanged; Style Aggregator is straightforward cross-attention replacement; voxelization borrowed from AnySplat; geometry/style heads are standard designs. Contribution feels like incremental engineering rather than fundamental innovation

Unfair baseline comparisons: StyleRF/StyleGS are per-scene trained versus Stylos's DL3DV-pretrained model—fundamentally different problem settings. Concurrent work Styl3R missing due to code unavailability, undermining SOTA claims. StyleRF results incomplete (marked '–') and some values appear anomalous (0.78 ArtScore)

Scalability claims contradicted by evidence: Abstract claims 'scaling to hundreds of views' but Fig. 4 shows clear degradation beyond 32 views with 'edge artifacts' at 64 views. Training limited to ≤24 views indicates domain gap for tested regime

Marginal improvements from 3D loss: Table 2 shows only ~5% improvement over scene loss (0.140 vs 0.147 LPIPS long-range), which does not strongly justify added complexity. No ablation on voxel grid resolution or theoretical justification for voxel space superiority

Two-stage training design poorly justified: Stage 1 uses random color-jittering as style reference without motivation; Stage 2 freezes geometry modules without ablation. No sensitivity analysis to Stage 1 quality; unclear if end-to-end training was attempted

Generalization claims overstate scope: 'Zero-shot' requires large DL3DV-10K pretraining; test sets (CO3D, Tanks and Temples) likely overlap DL3DV distribution. Cross-dataset generalization not demonstrated; performance degradation with limited training data not explored

Critical evaluation limitations: Consistency metrics computed on held-out views from same scenes (not true cross-scene consistency); ArtScore reliability not established; no user studies for subjective quality; missing computational cost analysis versus baselines

Incomplete technical specifications: Missing code URL (page 1); hyperparameter values (λ weights) not fully specified; training details (batch size, learning rates, duration, GPUs) absent; no sensitivity analysis for loss weights

Unresolved technical claims: Assertion that 'global cross-attention benefits geometric preservation' (abstract) lacks explanation or empirical validation—geometry pathway uses only self-attention, so how does style-side cross-attention help? Missing ablation validating this claim
No failure analysis: No discussion of failure cases, per-category performance differences, or conditions where method breaks down on complex scenes

strengths: Novel and principled 3D voxel-based style loss that effectively addresses multi-view consistency by operating in 3D feature space rather than 2D images
Well-designed dual-pathway architecture elegantly separating geometry (self-attention) from style (global cross-attention), with clear empirical validation through ablations
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three datasets with proper cross-category and cross-scene generalization tests, demonstrating consistent improvements over recent baselines
Zero-shot generalization capability with no per-scene optimization required, showing practical utility for real-world 3D content creation applications
Rigorous ablation studies (Tables 1-2, Figures 2-3) that clearly isolate and justify each design choice
Strong reproducibility practices including pseudo-code in appendix, promised code release, and clear use of public datasets
Clear presentation with well-designed figures, informative qualitative results, and thorough appendix with additional visual validation
weaknesses: Significant gap between claims and demonstration: paper claims to 'scale from single to hundreds of views' but Figure 4 shows substantial quality degradation beyond 32 views, inadequately explained as training domain gap
Missing comparison with most directly comparable concurrent work (Styl3R) due to code unavailability, limiting assessment of relative performance in equivalent setting

Geometric preservation claims rely primarily on consistency metrics rather than direct geometric accuracy evaluation; quantitative comparison of 3D geometry against ground truth would strengthen claims
Limited theoretical justification for design choices; why global cross-attention specifically preserves geometry better than frame-level attention needs deeper analysis beyond empirical results
Insufficient analysis of failure modes, sensitivity to loss weight hyperparameters, and performance under challenging VGGT conditions (difficult lighting, poses)
Comparison fairness concern: zero-shot feed-forward model compared against per-scene optimization methods; per-scene methods naturally trade off generalization for single-scene quality
Critical training details missing: training time, model size, memory requirements, sensitivity to loss weights, and justification for design choices like color-jittering not provided
Stylization quality evaluation relies on reference-free ArtScore metric without user studies; subjective visual assessment in Figure 5 alone may not be sufficient
Technical novelty is moderate; primarily combines existing components (VGGT, Transformer, statistics-based losses, 3DGS) with 3D loss being an incremental extension of existing statistical losses
Voxelization procedure underspecified: grid resolution selection, sensitivity analysis, and comparison to alternative 3D aggregation strategies not discussed

strengths: Well-motivated dual-pathway architecture that cleanly separates geometry and style through self-attention and global cross-attention respectively
Novel voxel-based 3D style loss extending 2D methods to enforce view-consistent stylization in 3D space
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (CO3D, DL3DV-10K, Tanks & Temples) with thorough baselines and multiple evaluation metrics
Strong practical results: achieves best/near-best consistency scores, dramatic speedup (0.05s vs 14.7-165 min), and zero-shot generalization to unseen categories/scenes/styles
Excellent reproducibility: detailed architecture description, pseudo-code, implementation details, promised code release, and extensive ablations
Extensive qualitative results and honest failure analysis demonstrating versatility and limitations
Clean experimental design with ablations on attention strategies validating design choices
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individually uses existing components (VGGT backbone, standard cross-attention, adapted existing style losses); contribution is primarily in their combination

Marginal empirical gains from proposed 3D loss: Table 2 shows short-range LPIPS unchanged (0.047→0.047), RMSE improvement of only 0.002, ArtScore gain of merely 0.03, undermining the significance of this core contribution

Scalability contradicts claims: performance degrades beyond 32 views/batch despite claims of handling 'hundreds of views'; training limited to ≤24 views; acknowledged VGGT instability with more views is fundamental limitation

Heavy dependence on VGGT backbone limits future impact; geometry quality bottlenecked by VGGT's reconstruction capability; tight coupling reduces modularity and limits improvements without backbone replacement
Incomplete positioning relative to closest work (Styl3R): limited quantitative comparison, claims about multi-view consistency lack substantiation, and gap between methods not thoroughly analyzed

Significant documented failure cases: struggles with high-frequency structures (thin branches, dense foliage), extreme lighting/color palettes, color hallucination, and over-smoothing—these are non-trivial practical limitations

No user study validation of stylization perceptual quality; reliance on relatively new metrics (ArtScore, ArtFID) without established validation; LPIPS/RMSE consistency metrics measure frame differences, not perceptual consistency

Experimental setup concerns: different input resolutions for baseline comparison (256×256 for Styl3R vs 448×448 for Stylos) complicates fair assessment; some baselines retrained rather than using official implementations

Insufficient analysis of design choices: limited explanation of why global cross-attention preserves details; only three attention variants tested; no ablation on voxelization strategy or CLIP loss contribution
Stage 1 training uses color-jittered content as style—pragmatic but unjustified; potential interaction between geometry and style quality during stage 2 not analyzed

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablations and comparisons across multiple datasets (CO3D, DL3DV-10K, Tanks & Temples)
Practical single-forward inference for instant 3D stylization without per-scene optimization
Solid empirical results achieving best consistency metrics (LPIPS, RMSE) on tested benchmarks
Clear ablation studies (Tables 1-2) systematically analyzing design choices
Reproducibility effort with promised code release and detailed architectural descriptions
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (VGGT, standard cross-attention, voxel aggregation); core contributions are incremental extensions of prior work (statistics-based losses, Transformer architectures)

Overstated claims: 'zero-shot generalization' is standard train-test splitting (not zero-shot); 'scaling to hundreds of views' contradicted by Fig. 4 showing degradation at 64 views and training limited to ≤24 views
Marginal improvements from proposed components: Table 2 shows negligible differences between scene and 3D losses (ArtScore: 9.12 vs 9.15); voxel-based loss improvement is within noise margins

Heavy dependence on VGGT with geometry modules frozen in Stage 2, making it unclear how much success is attributable to VGGT vs. the style pathway; acknowledged limitations stem from VGGT backbone, not Stylos
Significant unresolved failure modes (Appendix A.5, Figs. 11-13) including reconstruction errors, hallucinated colors, and over-smoothing, suggesting limited practical applicability
No mechanistic explanation for why voxel aggregation improves consistency; claim that global cross-attention 'preserves fine details' lacks support
Lacks perceptual validation: no user studies, relies entirely on automated metrics (LPIPS, ArtScore) without human evaluation of stylization quality
Design choices insufficiently justified: two-stage training strategy not ablated; why freeze geometry in Stage 2? Could joint optimization work?
Limited comparison with most relevant baseline (Styl3R): different design scopes (2-8 vs ~24 views) make direct comparison unfair; both methods degrade with many views

strengths: Clear practical contribution achieving real-time stylization (0.05s, 3300× speedup) without per-scene optimization
Novel voxel-based 3D style loss extending AdaIN to fused 3D space for multi-view consistency—well-motivated and shows consistent improvements
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (CO3D, DL3DV-10K, Tanks & Temples) with thorough ablations isolating design choices
Strong empirical results: best or competitive on consistency metrics across all scenes (Table 3) and artistic quality (Table 4) while being fastest
Well-motivated dual-pathway architecture with clear ablation evidence (Table 1) that global cross-attention outperforms alternatives
Thorough presentation with detailed architecture, comprehensive appendix with implementation details and promised code release
Demonstrates genuine zero-shot generalization to unseen categories, scenes, and styles with reproducible experiments using public datasets
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: geometry backbone directly from VGGT, style aggregator uses standard CrossBlocks, style losses extend existing methods—primarily combining existing components rather than introducing fundamentally new techniques

Heavy unresolved dependency on VGGT backbone: acknowledged limitation that performance degrades with increasing views due to VGGT; claims to handle hundreds of views contradicted by Figure 4 showing degradation at 64 views (trained on ≤24 views); unclear how much improvement is from Stylos vs. VGGT

Insufficient analysis of voxel-based loss: Algorithm 1 is straightforward reprojection+statistics; intuition for why voxelization specifically helps is unexplored; improvement over scene-level loss is modest (ArtScore 9.12→9.15 in Table 2); voxel size not ablated
No user study evaluation despite stylization being inherently subjective; relies on relatively new and unvalidated metrics (ArtScore, ArtFID) for artistic quality assessment
Incomplete architectural details: tokenization of images unclear, camera parameter incorporation not explained, patch embedding and DINOv2 usage not detailed—impacts reproducibility
Missing training efficiency analysis: only inference time reported; total wall-clock training time on DL3DV-10K not provided; two-stage training adds complexity
Hyperparameter sensitivity unexplored: loss weights fixed with no ablation; why are specific values chosen and how sensitive is performance to these choices?
Unclear comparison with Styl3R: both handle different view ranges but precise advantages of Stylos beyond multi-view consistency not clearly isolated

Disentanglement claims overstated: paper claims to disentangle geometry and style but only separates processing pathways; no analysis of actual feature disentanglement or whether influence occurs during rendering
